newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia news agency loses rights over foreign news.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia news agency loses rights over foreign news.

text.p: Malaysia has decided to withdraw the controls over foreign news and news vendors that it had given to the national news agency Bernama, Information Minister Mohamed Rahmat said on Wednesday.
The cabinet decided at its weekly meeting to allow a free flow of information in line with the promotion of government's "Multimedia Super Corridor", Mohamed told reporters.
Steps would be taken to amend the Bernama Act to end the controls by the agency, he said.
"Under the existing Act, the flow of foreign news into Malaysia is required to go through Bernama," he told reporters.
The act gives Bernama the power to distribute foreign news agency stories and information to clients in Malaysia, for which it charges fees.
Bernama is one of several news agencies in Asia that have had this arrangement, along with Indonesia's Antara and China's Xinhua.

Malaysia is promoting the Multimedia Super Corridor as a haven for global information technology companies. The 15-by-50-km (9.3-by-31-mile) zone stretches from Kuala Lumpur south to where a new airport and federal capital are under construction.
Mohamed said his ministry was working with the attorney-general to draft the amendments, which he hoped to bring to the cabinet as soon as possible before being tabled in Parliament.

He said that with the scrapping of its special rights, foreign news agencies and other information providers would be free to channel news and information direct to subscribers in Malaysia, bypassing Bernama.
